sup-36fca83b088ab7dc-q91:whole.hint: Which observer measures the object at rest? That observer measures its proper length.
notes: For length parallel to the relative motion, L = L₀/γ. L₀ is the rest length; perpendicular dimensions are unchanged.
Measuring length in a frame requires positions of both ends at the same time in that frame. Do not combine one frame’s distance with another frame’s time.

sup-36fca83b088ab7dc-q92:whole.hint: Identify the frame in which the two events happen at the same place. Its clock measures the proper time.
notes: Time dilation is Δt = γΔτ, with γ = 1/√(1 − v²/c²). Proper time is measured by one clock present at both events.
Use distances and speeds measured in the same frame. If a journey time is L/v in the Earth frame, the travelling clock records that interval divided by γ.

sup-36fca83b088ab7dc-q93:whole.hint: Which observer measures the object at rest? That observer measures its proper length.
notes: For length parallel to the relative motion, L = L₀/γ. L₀ is the rest length; perpendicular dimensions are unchanged.
Measuring length in a frame requires positions of both ends at the same time in that frame. Do not combine one frame’s distance with another frame’s time.

sup-36fca83b088ab7dc-q94:whole.hint: Draw the velocities with their reference frames labelled. Which two vectors combine to give the required motion?
notes: At non-relativistic speeds, v(A relative to C) = v(A relative to B) + v(B relative to C). Resolve perpendicular directions separately.
For a magnitude and direction, combine the components using Pythagoras and a labelled angle. Do not add the magnitudes of perpendicular velocities.

sup-36fca83b088ab7dc-q95:whole.hint: At speeds comparable with c, ordinary addition of velocities is no longer valid.
notes: For collinear motion, u′ = (u − v)/(1 − uv/c²), with signed velocities. Use the inverse relation for the opposite transformation.
Check the low-speed limit and that a light signal still has speed c. A result exceeding c for a material object indicates a sign or formula error.

sup-36fca83b088ab7dc-q96:whole.hint: At speeds comparable with c, ordinary addition of velocities is no longer valid.
notes: For collinear motion, u′ = (u − v)/(1 − uv/c²), with signed velocities. Use the inverse relation for the opposite transformation.
Check the low-speed limit and that a light signal still has speed c. A result exceeding c for a material object indicates a sign or formula error.

sup-36fca83b088ab7dc-q97:whole.hint: Write down the position and time of each event in the frame where they are given before transforming them.
notes: For S′ moving at +v relative to S, x′ = γ(x − vt) and t′ = γ(t − vx/c²). Use the inverse transformation, with +v, to go from S′ to S.
Simultaneity depends on the frame for spatially separated events. On a spacetime diagram, check whether the time axis is t or ct before reading slopes.

sup-36fca83b088ab7dc-q98:whole.hint: Check whether the axes are x and ct, then locate events whose coordinates you can transform.
notes: On a spacetime diagram, the moving frame axes are tilted, and their scale marks cannot be copied by ordinary perpendicular projection.
